d: the relatively deep area of the sea or ocean sufficiently far from land as to be beyond the range of any protection from the seacoast
a generic collective term for all bodies of water (in this sense θάλασσα[a] is contrasted with the sky and the land)
a part of the sea which is partially enclosed by land
a relatively small area of the sea which is well protected by land but deep enough for ships to enter and moor
a relatively small body of water either natural or artificial, surrounded by land
pertaining to being located beside the sea or along the shore
the relatively deep area of the sea or ocean sufficiently far from land as to be beyond the range of any protection from the seacoast
a source of water flowing onto the surface or into a pool somewhat below ground level
a river or stream normally flowing throughout the year (in contrast with {L:χείμαρρος<SDBG:χείμαρρος:000001>}[b] ‘winter stream,’ {D:1.77})

a stream or river which flows only during the rainy season (in Palestine this would be during the winter months) or when melting snow from the mountains provides running water for a relatively short period of time
